newsitem.title: UK: NWE physical gas oil pushes IPE to five year high.
newsitem.headline: NWE physical gas oil pushes IPE to five year high.

text.p: NWE gas oil was firmer despite a lack of physical trade on Tuesday as IPE futures made new five-year highs on the back of strong fundamentals.
Although the ARA heating oil market was quiet, German inland dealers complained of a lack of product to meet end-user demand.
The diesel market was also seen tight on the first day that EU rules for low sulphur fuel came into force at the pumps.
"The market can't survive without buying for more than two or three days," said an ARA refiner.
Low sulphur diesel accounts for about a third of the 400,000 tonnes or more of gas oil headed to NWE from the U.S.
Traders said the arb was still open, although low stocks continue to push U.S. physical and futures prices higher.
Heat barges traded at Oct IPE +$8.25 fob R'dam, and cargoes were bid at $8 and offered at $10 a tonne cif Hamburg. A small parcel was traded into Poland at a quotes-related price.

Low sulphur diesel was around Nov IPE +$20 cif NWE after a cargo traded into Rostock on Monday at Nov +$20.50, but most sellers were reluctant to talk Nov given the $11 backwardation on Oct/Nov futures. Small 0.1 percent Russian cargoes were offered at quotes high +$3/$4 cif NWE.
